paper: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
dataset: The paper is not about liver segmentation. It evaluates on: 1) ISBI EM segmentation challenge (30 serial section transmission electron microscopy images of Drosophila larva ventral nerve cord, 512x512 pixels); 2) PhC-U373 (35 phase contrast microscopy images of Glioblastoma-astrocytoma cells); and 3) DIC-HeLa (20 differential interference contrast microscopy images of HeLa cells).
method: A symmetric u-shaped fully convolutional network that combines a contracting path to capture context with an expansive path using skip connections to enable precise localization, optimized for training from very few images using elastic deformation data augmentation.
metric: Warping Error, Rand Error, Pixel Error, and Average Intersection over Union (IOU)
result: Achieved a warping error of 0.000353 and a Rand error of 0.0382 on the EM segmentation challenge. On the ISBI cell tracking challenge, it achieved average IOUs of 92.03% (0.9203) on the PhC-U373 dataset and 77.56% (0.7756) on the DIC-HeLa dataset.
limitation: The paper does not address liver segmentation. A technical limitation is that the use of unpadded convolutions results in an output segmentation map that is smaller than the input image, requiring an overlap-tile strategy and boundary mirroring extrapolation to handle arbitrarily large images.

paper: Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas
dataset: Two datasets: CT-150 (150 3D abdominal CT scans) and TCIA Pancreas-CT/CT-82 (82 contrast-enhanced 3D CT scans). Note: This paper is not about liver segmentation, and no liver-specific segmentation performance is reported.
method: Integrates self-attention gates (AGs) into the standard U-Net skip connections to automatically focus on target structures of varying shapes and sizes by suppressing feature activations in irrelevant background regions.
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Mesh Surface-to-Surface (S2S) distance (mm), Precision, Recall
result: On the CT-150 dataset (120/30 split), the Attention U-Net achieved a pancreas DSC of 0.840 ± 0.087 and an S2S distance of 1.920 ± 1.284 mm. On the TCIA dataset, it achieved a 5-fold cross-validation pancreas DSC of 81.48 ± 6.23%.
limitation: The paper does not investigate or report results on liver segmentation. Additionally, input images had to be downsampled to isotropic 2.00 mm resolution due to GPU memory limitations, and no post-processing (such as CRFs) was utilized.

paper: UNet++: A Nested U-Net Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: Four datasets: cell nuclei (670 microscopy images, 96x96), colon polyp (7,379 RGB video frames, 224x224), liver (331 CT scans, 512x512 from MICCAI 2018 LiTS Challenge), and lung nodule (1,012 CT scans, 64x64x64)
method: A deeply-supervised encoder-decoder network where nested, dense skip pathways connect the encoder and decoder sub-networks to reduce the semantic gap between their feature maps.
metric: Intersection over Union (IoU) in %
result: UNet++ with deep supervision achieved IoU scores of 92.52% on cell nuclei, 32.12% on colon polyp, 82.90% on liver, and 77.21% on lung nodule, outperforming the standard U-Net which achieved 90.77%, 30.08%, 76.62%, and 71.47% respectively.
limitation: The performance improvement from deep supervision vanishes for cell nuclei and colon polyp segmentation, and aggressive pruning of the model at inference time to achieve speed gains results in significant accuracy degradation.

paper: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: The Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) challenge, consisting of 10 distinct tasks of varying sizes and modalities (including CT for Liver, Lung, Pancreas, and MRI for BrainTumour, Heart, Hippocampus, Prostate). The paper proposes a general-purpose framework and is not primarily focused on liver segmentation.
model: nnU-Net (including 2D U-Net, 3D U-Net, and a U-Net Cascade)
method: A self-adapting framework that automatically configures network topology, preprocessing, training, and inference choices to specialize vanilla U-Nets to any given medical image dataset without human intervention.
metric: Mean Dice score
result: On the MSD Liver test set, nnU-Net achieved Dice scores of 95.24% for class 1 (liver) and 73.71% for class 2 (tumor), via the 3D U-Net + U-Net Cascade ensemble (Table 2) - the highest score on the public leaderboard at submission time for liver and 6 other tasks.
limitation: Training and cross-validating three distinct model configurations (2D, 3D, and Cascade) for each dataset to select the best one is computationally demanding, and several specific design choices (such as Leaky ReLUs and data augmentation parameters) were not validated via ablation studies.

paper: The Liver Tumor Segmentation Benchmark (LiTS)
dataset: LiTS (Liver Tumor Segmentation Benchmark) consisting of 201 abdominal CT volumes (131 training and 70 testing) showing primary and secondary tumors with varied sizes and appearances.
model: Various submitted architectures, predominantly U-Net-based (including nn-UNet, H-DenseUNet, and 2D/2.5D/3D cascaded residual U-Nets).
method: A multi-center benchmarking challenge evaluating 75 liver and liver tumor segmentation and detection algorithms across three events (ISBI 2017, MICCAI 2017, and MICCAI 2018).
metric: Dice score, Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASD), Maximum Symmetric Surface Distance (MSSD), Relative Volume Difference (RVD), Precision, Recall, and F1-score.
result: The best liver segmentation achieved a Dice score of 0.963. The best liver tumor segmentation achieved Dice scores of 0.674 (ISBI 2017), 0.702 (MICCAI 2017), and 0.739 (MICCAI 2018). The best tumor detection achieved lesion-wise recall of 0.458 (ISBI 2017), 0.515 (MICCAI 2017), and 0.554 (MICCAI 2018).
limitation: No single algorithm performed best for both liver and liver tumors, and all methods struggled significantly with small tumors (under 10 mm in diameter) and cases with low contrast difference (below 20 HU) between liver and tumor.

paper: 3D U-Net: Learning Dense Volumetric Segmentation from Sparse Annotation
dataset: Three 3D confocal microscopy volumes of Xenopus kidney embryos (not about liver segmentation), with down-sampled sizes of approximately 245x244x56 to 248x244x64 voxels.
method: The method generalizes the 2D U-Net to a 3D architecture using 3D convolutions, max pooling, and up-convolutions, trained end-to-end with a weighted softmax loss function that allows learning from sparse annotations.
metric: Intersection over Union (IoU)
result: For semi-automated segmentation, the network with batch normalization achieved an average IoU of 0.863. For fully-automated segmentation, the network achieved an average IoU of 0.704 with batch normalization and 0.723 without batch normalization.
limitation: The paper does not address liver segmentation. Additionally, batch normalization was counterproductive in the fully-automated setup for the third test volume, dropping the IoU from 0.779 to 0.554 due to high variability between the small number of available dataset samples.

paper: V-Net: Fully Convolutional Neural Networks for Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: PROMISE2012 challenge dataset consisting of 50 training and 30 test MRI volumes of the prostate (the paper is not about liver segmentation).
method: An end-to-end 3D fully convolutional neural network utilizing volumetric convolutions, residual connections, and a novel Dice coefficient-based loss function to address class imbalance.
metric: Average Dice coefficient, Average Hausdorff distance (mm), and PROMISE2012 challenge score
result: V-Net with Dice-based loss achieved an Average Dice of 0.869 +/- 0.033, an Average Hausdorff distance of 5.71 +/- 1.20 mm, and a PROMISE2012 challenge score of 82.39.
limitation: The model has high memory requirements during training which restricted the mini-batch size to only two volumes, and it was not evaluated on liver segmentation.

paper: H-DenseUNet: Hybrid Densely Connected UNet for Liver and Tumor Segmentation from CT Volumes
dataset: MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset (131 training and 70 testing volumes) and 3DIRCADb dataset (20 volumes), both consisting of contrast-enhanced 3D abdominal CT scans
model: H-DenseUNet (Hybrid Densely Connected UNet), consisting of 2D DenseUNet-167 and 3D DenseUNet-65
method: The method extracts high-level intra-slice representations using a deep 2D DenseUNet and aggregates volumetric context using a 3D DenseUNet, jointly optimizing them through a hybrid feature fusion layer.
metric: Dice per case, Dice global, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Volumetric Overlap Error (VOE), Relative Volume Difference (RVD), Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASD), and Root Mean Square symmetric surface distance (RMSD)
result: On the LiTS test dataset, H-DenseUNet achieved a Dice per case of 72.2% for lesion and 96.1% for liver, and a Dice global of 82.4% for lesion and 96.5% for liver. Tested on the 3DIRCADb dataset (using LiTS as additional training data), it achieved a Dice of 93.7% for tumor and 98.2% for liver.
limitation: The segmentation improvement for small tumors is limited because they occur in fewer slices, and the network's potential depth and model complexity are restricted by GPU memory limitations.

paper: Automatic Liver and Tumor Segmentation of CT and MRI Volumes using Cascaded Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
dataset: 3DIRCADb (20 venous phase CT volumes, 15 with tumors), a multicentric clinical CT dataset (100 scans), and a clinical DW-MRI dataset (31 patients)
model: Cascaded Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (CFCN) based on U-Net, combined with a 3D Dense Conditional Random Field (CRF)
method: Two fully convolutional networks are cascaded sequentially to first segment the liver as a region of interest (ROI) and then segment lesions within that ROI, with final refinement using a 3D dense conditional random field.
metric: Dice score (DICE), Volume Overlap Error (VOE), Relative Volume Difference (RVD), Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASD), and Symmetric Maximum Surface Distance (MSD)
result: On 3DIRCADb, Cascaded U-Net + 3D CRF achieved a liver Dice score of 94.3% and a lesion Dice score of 56% plus/minus 26%. On the clinical CT dataset, it achieved a liver Dice of 91% and lesion Dice of 61% plus/minus 25%. On clinical MR-DWI, it achieved a liver Dice of 87% and lesion Dice of 69.7%.
limitation: Tuning the hyperparameters of the 3D CRF is highly time-consuming and task-dependent, making it difficult to find a hyperparameter set that generalizes well to unseen, highly heterogeneous cases such as HCC lesions.

paper: The Medical Segmentation Decathlon
dataset: The Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD), containing 10 heterogeneous datasets (brain, liver, heart, hippocampus, prostate, lung, pancreas, colon, hepatic vessels, spleen) with 2,633 total CT and MRI volumes. Note: this paper is not primarily about liver segmentation.
model: nnU-Net (modified U-Net with leaky ReLU, instance normalization, and strided convolutions)
method: nnU-Net dynamically and automatically configures its entire segmentation pipeline (including pre-processing, network architecture, and post-processing) independently for each task based on the characteristics of the training dataset.
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Normalised Surface Distance (NSD)
result: The challenge winner, nnU-Net, achieved a median DSC of 0.79 (IQR: 0.61, 0.88) in the development phase and 0.71 (IQR: 0.58, 0.82) in the mystery phase across all tasks, specifically obtaining a mean DSC of 0.93 for liver and 0.74 for liver tumor.
limitation: The MSD dataset relies on retrospectively collected and labeled data with heterogeneous protocols, lacks multi-rater annotations for most tasks, is restricted entirely to radiological modalities, and the study is not primarily focused on liver segmentation specifically.

paper: A large annotated medical image dataset for the development and evaluation of segmentation algorithms
dataset: Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) dataset, including Task03_Liver (201 contrast-enhanced 3D CT scans) and Task08_HepaticVessel (443 portal venous phase 3D CT scans), alongside 8 other diverse medical datasets totaling 2,633 images.
model: None (this is a data descriptor paper and does not introduce or evaluate a specific segmentation model)
method: The paper presents the collection, curation, de-identification, and standardized reformatting of ten multi-institutional, open-source medical imaging datasets into NIfTI format with a standard RAS coordinate frame.
metric: None
result: Not applicable (the paper describes the release of the dataset collection for the 2018 MICCAI Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge and does not report model performance results)
limitation: The paper is not primarily about developing a liver segmentation method, but rather presents a dataset repository; limitations of the repository include potential coordinate transformation errors introduced during DICOM-to-NIfTI conversion (requiring manual verification) and substantial protocol and scanner variability across participating institutions.

paper: TransUNet: Transformers Make Strong Encoders for Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: The paper is evaluated on two datasets: 1) Synapse multi-organ segmentation dataset consisting of 30 abdominal CT scans (3779 clinical axial CT slices) where liver is one of 8 organs; 2) Automated Cardiac Diagnosis Challenge (ACDC) dataset consisting of cine MR images from 100 patients. The paper is not primarily about liver segmentation, but includes it in the multi-organ dataset.
method: TransUNet combines a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture as the encoder to leverage both high-resolution CNN feature maps and global context from Transformers, and connects it to a cascaded upsampler (CUP) via U-Net-like skip connections to recover fine spatial details.
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC in %) and Hausdorff Distance (HD in mm)
result: On the Synapse multi-organ CT dataset (using 224x224 input resolution), TransUNet achieved an average DSC of 77.48% (with a liver-specific DSC of 94.08%) and an average HD of 31.69 mm. On the ACDC cardiac MRI dataset, it achieved an average DSC of 89.71% (88.86% RV, 84.53% Myo, 95.73% LV).
limitation: The paper is not primarily focused on liver segmentation but rather multi-organ and cardiac segmentation. Additionally, achieving optimal performance requires a high input resolution of 512x512 (improving average DSC to 84.36% from 77.48%), which comes at the expense of a much larger computational cost, and incorporating heavier Transformer layers in the skip-connections is restricted by GPU memory constraints.

paper: Swin-Unet: Unet-like Pure Transformer for Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: Synapse multi-organ CT dataset (30 cases, 3779 abdominal CT slices) and ACDC cardiac MRI dataset (100 cases, MRI modality). Note that the paper is not primarily focused on liver segmentation but includes it as one of eight abdominal organs.
method: A symmetric U-shaped encoder-decoder medical image segmentation network constructed entirely from Swin Transformer blocks, using skip connections and a newly proposed patch expanding layer to perform up-sampling without convolution.
metric: Dice-Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff Distance (HD)
result: Swin-Unet achieved an average DSC of 79.13% and HD of 21.55 on the Synapse dataset (with a liver-specific DSC of 94.29%), and an average DSC of 90.00% on the ACDC dataset.
limitation: The model is restricted to 2D image slices whereas most clinical medical image data is 3D, and its representation capability relies heavily on ImageNet pre-training which may be suboptimal for medical imaging modalities.

paper: nnFormer: Interleaved Transformer for Volumetric Segmentation
dataset: Three volumetric medical image datasets: MSD Brain Tumor Segmentation (484 multi-channel MRI scans), Synapse multi-organ segmentation (30 abdominal CT scans), and ACDC (100 cardiac MRI scans). The paper is not primarily focused on liver segmentation.
method: A 3D transformer architecture for volumetric medical image segmentation that interleaves convolution and self-attention layers, utilizes local and global volume-based self-attention, and replaces standard skip connections with a skip attention mechanism.
metric: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) in % and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) in mm
result: On the Synapse abdominal CT dataset, nnFormer achieved a liver segmentation DSC of 96.84% and an HD95 of 2.00 mm, outperforming transformer-based baselines like UNETR (94.46% DSC) but slightly underperforming the convolutional nnUNet (97.23% DSC, 1.62 mm HD95).
limitation: The paper is not primarily about liver segmentation. Furthermore, nnFormer underperforms the CNN-based nnUNet on several abdominal organs (including the liver, aorta, gallbladder, and spleen) in DSC, indicating that pure transformer approaches still struggle to consistently outperform optimized CNN baselines on all organ structures without ensembling.

paper: UNETR: Transformers for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: BTCV (30 abdominal CT scans, multi-organ including liver), MSD Brain Tumor (484 multi-modal MRI scans), and MSD Spleen (41 CT scans). This paper is not primarily about liver segmentation.
method: The method reformulates 3D medical image segmentation as a sequence-to-sequence prediction task using a transformer encoder to learn global contextual representations, which are connected to a CNN decoder via multi-scale skip connections.
metric: Dice similarity coefficient (Dice) and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95)
result: On the BTCV Standard Competition, UNETR achieved an average Dice score of 0.853 (with a Liver-specific Dice of 0.971). On MSD Spleen, it achieved a Dice of 0.964 and HD95 of 1.333. On MSD Brain Tumor, it achieved WT Dice of 0.789, ET Dice of 0.585, and TC Dice of 0.761.
limitation: This paper is not primarily about liver segmentation. Furthermore, a major limitation is high GPU memory consumption at lower patch resolutions (since sequence length scales inversely with the cube of the patch resolution), which restricted the authors from experimenting with patch resolutions below 16x16x16.

paper: ResUNet++: An Advanced Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: Kvasir-SEG (1,000 polyp images, 2D colonoscopy RGB) and CVC-ClinicDB/CVC-612 (612 images, 2D colonoscopy RGB). Note: This paper is not primarily about liver segmentation.
method: An advanced medical image segmentation architecture that integrates residual blocks, squeeze-and-excitation units, Atrous Spatial Pyramidal Pooling (ASPP), and attention blocks into a U-Net backbone.
metric: Dice coefficient, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), Recall, Precision
result: On Kvasir-SEG: Dice of 81.33% (0.8133), mIoU of 79.27% (0.7927), Recall of 70.64%, and Precision of 87.74%. On CVC-612: Dice of 79.55% (0.7955), mIoU of 79.62% (0.7962), Recall of 70.22%, and Precision of 87.85%.
limitation: The proposed architecture uses more parameters which increases training time, requires image resizing which may cause a loss of useful information, and the paper does not address liver segmentation.

paper: DoubleU-Net: A Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Medical Image Segmentation
dataset: The paper is not primarily about liver segmentation; it evaluates four datasets: 2015 MICCAI automatic polyp detection dataset (808 colonoscopy images, 384x288), CVC-ClinicDB (612 colonoscopy images, 384x288), Lesion Boundary Segmentation challenge from ISIC-2018 (2594 dermoscopy images, variable size), and 2018 Data Science Bowl challenge (670 nuclei microscopy images, 256x256).
method: DoubleU-Net combines two U-Net architectures stacked sequentially, utilizing a pre-trained VGG-19 encoder in the first network, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP), and squeeze-and-excite blocks to improve medical image segmentation.
metric: Sørensen-Dice coefficient (DSC), mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), Precision, and Recall
result: DoubleU-Net achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.7649 and mIoU of 0.6255 on the 2015 MICCAI dataset, DSC of 0.9239 and mIoU of 0.8611 on CVC-ClinicDB, DSC of 0.8962 and mIoU of 0.8212 on the ISIC-2018 lesion dataset, and DSC of 0.9133 on the 2018 Data Science Bowl dataset.
limitation: DoubleU-Net uses more parameters compared to standard U-Net, which leads to an increase in training time.

paper: 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation using autoencoder regularization
dataset: BraTS 2018 training dataset consisting of 285 cases (210 HGG and 75 LGG), each with four 3D MRI modalities (T1, T1c, T2, FLAIR) of size 240x240x155
model: Encoder-decoder CNN with an additional variational autoencoder (VAE) regularization branch
method: A semantic segmentation network uses an asymmetrically large encoder and a VAE reconstruction branch during training to regularize the shared encoder and impose additional constraints on its layers.
metric: Dice score and Hausdorff distance
result: On the BraTS 2018 testing dataset, an ensemble of 10 models achieved average dice scores of 0.7664, 0.8839, and 0.8154 for the enhancing tumor core, whole tumor, and tumor core respectively.
limitation: The paper is about brain tumor segmentation, not liver segmentation, and requires high GPU memory limits which restrict the batch size to 1 when using larger crop sizes.

paper: Generalised Dice overlap as a deep learning loss function for highly unbalanced segmentations
dataset: BRATS dataset (2D) and an in-house dataset of 524 subjects with age-related white matter hyperintensities (3D, T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and FLAIR)
method: We propose using the class re-balancing properties of the Generalized Dice overlap as a robust and accurate deep-learning loss function for unbalanced segmentation tasks.
metric: Dice Score Coefficient (DSC)
result: In the 3D white matter hyperintensities task using HighResNet at a learning rate of 10^-4 with the largest patch size, GDLv achieved superior segmentation performance compared to DL2 and SS, capturing punctuate lesions more effectively where WCE failed to train.
limitation: The study was not primarily evaluated on liver segmentation, focusing instead on brain tumor and white matter hyperintensity segmentation, and tested networks without training data augmentation.

paper: The state of the art in kidney and kidney tumor segmentation in contrast-enhanced CT imaging: Results of the KiTS19 Challenge
dataset: KiTS19 challenge dataset comprising 300 cross-sectional CT images with kidney and kidney tumor segmentation masks (210 training, 90 test)
method: A vanilla 3D U-Net augmented with residual connections was trained using extensive data preprocessing and cross-entropy plus dice loss without transfer learning.
metric: Sørensen-Dice coefficient
result: The winning team achieved a Dice of 0.974 for kidney and 0.851 for tumor, resulting in a composite score of 0.912.
limitation: The dataset is retrospective and heavily concentrated in a limited geographic region from a single health system, which may limit generalizability.
